2. Place of Articulation: Where?

Orange = lips and teeth. • Green = front of the tongue. • Purple = back of the mouth.

Click any symbol to hear it
1 Bilabial
two lips
2 Labiodental
lip and top teeth
3 Dental
tongue tip and teeth
4 Alveolar
tongue and the ridge behind the teeth
5 Postalveolar
tongue just behind the ridge
6 Palatal
tongue and hard palate
7 Velar
back of tongue and soft palate
8 Glottal
between the vocal cords

4. Manner of Articulation: How?

The type tells us what happens to the air. Click any symbol to hear its sound.

Plosive

air is stopped, then let go

Nasal

air goes out through the nose

Fricative

air is pushed through a narrow gap

Affricate

a plosive, then a fricative (2 sounds)

Approximant

moves smoothly, no friction

VOWELS & SOUND CONCEPTS

English Vowels, Allophones & Word Relationships

New reference material, arranged in compact cards for easier phone reading.

1. Describe a vowel with 3 questions

How high is the tongue?

Close • Mid • Open

Which part of the tongue is highest?

Front • Central • Back

What shape are the lips?

Spread • Neutral • Rounded

2. Lip shape

Spread

Like a small smile

iː ɪ e æ
Neutral

Relaxed, not round

ʌ ɑː ɜː ə
Rounded

Like a small circle

ɒ ɔː ʊ uː

4. Short and long vowels

The mark ː means the vowel is long. Say it for longer.

ship /ɪ/short
sheep /iː/long
full /ʊ/short
fool /uː/long
cot /ɒ/short
caught /ɔː/long
cut /ʌ/short
cart /ɑː/long

6. Allophones

One phoneme can have different sounds. Each sound is an allophone. The meaning does not change.

pin → [pʰ]

A puff of air

spin → [p]

No puff of air

7. Homonyms & Homographs

Homonyms

Same spelling • Same sound • Different meaning

Example: bat; bank (as shown in the lecture)

Homographs

Same spelling • Different sound • Different meaning

Examples: lead, tear, wind; read, bow, minute, present, row

WordSound 1Sound 2
lead/liːd/ guide/led/ metal
tear/tɪə/ from eye/teə/ rip
wind/wɪnd/ air/waɪnd/ turn
bow/baʊ/ bow and arrow/bəʊ/ bend forward

8. Homophones

Words with the same sound but different spelling and meaning (practice often contrasts these).

pear → pairflower → flourwon → onerite → rightwhether → weatherweight → waitknew → newthrew → through
